name: seam
description: Decompose a diff into seams (core/link/environment/test/noise) and review by intent: seam colours on the native diff + a seam tree, powered by the Seam engine (TypeScript).

commands.title: Seam: Analyze module (all exports of this file)
Seam: Auto-map intent (LLM grows the footprint)…
Seam: Toggle chain view (symbol links + nature)

seam.toolPath.description: Absolute path to the code-review-sort checkout (containing the ts/ engine). Defaults to a bundled path if empty.

enumDescriptions: Default. LLM clustering (product intent) + deterministic roles & wiring, fed AST facts (defines/enclosing) from the editor's language server.
Fully deterministic, offline — no LLM at all (structural cluster labels instead of product-intent prose).
seam.engine.description: How to decompose a diff: 'hybrid' (LLM clusters + deterministic roles/wiring — best; needs a CLI for clustering), 'det' (fully offline, no LLM), or 'llm' (all LLM).

seam.codebaseDepth.description: Codebase mode (Analyze from anchor): how many call-graph hops to resolve outward from the anchor. Higher = more context but slower / larger (the anchor-bounded BFS depth).

enumDescriptions: Deterministic floor only (relative + package + tsconfig paths). Offline, instant.
A real language server (go-to-definition). Cross-language, needs the toolchain.
Default. LSP with deterministic fallback — the warm daemon is reused across reviews.
seam.resolver.description: How a diff review resolves references against the repo (for blast radius). 'auto' (LSP + floor fallback), 'det' (offline floor), or 'lsp' (server only).

seam.blastRadius.description: Diff review: show each changed symbol's blast radius — who OUTSIDE the diff imports it (resolved/suggested) — so the change is read in the context of the real codebase.

enumDescriptions: Start with a big cluster's sub-groups COLLAPSED — review the few groups first, expand the one you want.
Start with sub-groups EXPANDED — go straight to the seams.
seam.defaultAltitude.description: Diff review: the starting altitude when a large cluster is split into structural sub-groups. 'overview' (collapsed) or 'seams' (expanded). Expand/collapse a group any time to zoom in/out.
